extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners (attorneys and agents), applicants, and patent examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and quality/ procedural standards governing interviews with examiners and the manner, timing, and form of amendments to patent applications under 37 CFR 1.121 and related provisions. Covers who may participate in interviews, demo/exhibit handling, and detailed formatting/content requirements for specification, claim, and drawing amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner authorization for interviews (37 CFR 11.106)
rubrics_metrics.description: A registered practitioner cannot authorize other registered practitioners to conduct interviews unless the client gives informed consent; a practitioner should not authorize a non-practitioner to conduct interviews as that could be aiding in the unauthorized practice of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 11.106 and 11.505; even with informed consent, authorizing non-practitioners is discouraged and may violate 37 CFR 11.18 (disciplinary consequences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to file authorization/power of attorney prior to interview
rubrics_metrics.description: A registered practitioner not of record may request an interview only if authorized by the applicant or attorney of record; it is recommended that a power of attorney, Interview Request Form (PTOL-413A), or electronic authorization to act in a representative capacity be filed prior to the interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File electronically, preferably before the interview to establish authority to represent the applicant during the interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to bind principal required for granting interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews normally should not be granted unless the requesting party has authority to bind the principal concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of 37 CFR 1.34 by a third party or its representative to conduct an interview or take actions not specifically permitted will be treated as a violation of 37 CFR 11.18 and may result in disciplinary action. Ensure documented authority before proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner negotiation authority requirement in interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: For an interview with an examiner who does not have negotiation authority, arrangements should include an examiner who does have such authority and who is familiar with the application so authoritative agreement may be reached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always include personnel who can reach authoritative agreements during the interview to avoid delays; for remote grouped interviews ensure appropriate examiner participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouped interview practice for remote practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: Attorneys remote from Washington, D.C. who prefer in-person or video conference interviews can use the grouped interview practice; if agreement is reached, applicant should promptly submit an amendment pursuant to the agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grouped interviews are effective for remote practitioners; when agreement is reached, promptly file implementing amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: No ex parte discussion of inter partes questions
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may not discuss inter partes questions ex parte with any of the interested parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid discussing inter partes issues in ex parte interviews; such topics are outside permitted ex parte communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exposure of other cases/files during interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to an interview, the examiner should ensure that all files, drawings and other papers, except those necessary for the interview, are out of view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect confidentiality and avoid exposure of unrelated matters (see MPEP § 101).

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrations/exhibits/models usage and record rules (37 CFR 1.91; 1.133(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention may be exhibited or demonstrated by a model or exhibit during the interview; a model or exhibit used only for demonstration will not generally be admitted as part of the record unless it complies with 37 CFR 1.91.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a model/exhibit is submitted that complies with 37 CFR 1.91 it will be made part of the record. If used only for demonstration, it is not part of the record and a full description of what was demonstrated must be made of record (37 CFR 1.133(b)). Large exhibits may be viewed outside the Office with supervisory approval if essential to clarifying issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews after final rejection and prior to appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally one interview after final rejection is permitted to place the application in condition for allowance or to resolve issues prior to appeal; the intended purpose and content should be presented briefly, preferably in writing, before the interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant interviews only if the examiner is convinced that disposal or clarification for appeal can be accomplished with only nominal further consideration. Interviews that merely restate arguments or propose new limitations requiring more than nominal reconsideration or new search should be denied. A second or further interview may be held if the examiner believes it will expedite issues for appeal or disposal. See MPEP § 714.13 and § 706.07(f) for timing provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews after allowance regarding amendments (37 CFR 1.312)
rubrics_metrics.description: After an application is sent to issue (after a notice of allowance), interviews that involve detailed consideration of claims sought to be entered or prior art should not be given; requests for interviews in such cases should be granted only with specific approval of the Technology Center Director upon a written showing of extraordinary circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are not entitled to greater consideration for informally presented amendments than for formally presented ones; interviews after allowance are tightly constrained.

rubrics_metrics.name: General requirement to comply with 37 CFR 1.121 for amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: All amendments to applications (other than reissue) must comply with 37 CFR 1.121; amendments filed on or after July 30, 2003 must comply with revised 1.121 or the Office will issue a Notice of Non-Compliant Amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rules facilitate electronic image processing; failure to comply triggers non-compliance procedures. Follow the MPEP summary and detailed requirements to avoid processing delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment document sectioning and recommended format
rubrics_metrics.description: Each section of an amendment document (Specification Amendments, Claim Amendments, Drawing Amendments, Remarks) must begin on a separate sheet to facilitate indexing and scanning; recommended order: cover sheet (table of contents), 'Amendments to the Specification', 'Amendments to the Claims', 'Amendments to the Drawings', remarks section, and any drawing sheets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt this recommended format to reduce processing time and avoid non-compliant amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to the specification: methods and identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to the specification (other than claims and certain special appendices) must be made by adding, deleting, or replacing a paragraph; by replacing a section; or by providing a substitute specification. The amendment must unambiguously identify the paragraph or section to be modified by paragraph number, page and line, or other unambiguous method and be accompanied by replacement or new paragraphs as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement paragraphs must include markings to show all changes relative to previous version. Added paragraphs presented in clean form (no underlining). If paragraph numbering exists, maintain or use decimal numbering for inserted paragraphs (e.g., [0071.1]).

rubrics_metrics.name: Markings for replacement and added specification text
rubrics_metrics.description: For replacement paragraphs/sections the full text must be provided with markings to show changes: added subject matter shown by underlining; deleted matter shown by strike-through; deletions of five or fewer consecutive characters may use double brackets; if strike-through cannot be perceived, double brackets must be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added paragraphs (new subject matter) must be presented in clean form without underlining. A marked-up version is not required for deleted paragraphs; it is sufficient to identify which paragraph is deleted. Use square brackets [ ] for bracket terminology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute specification requirements (37 CFR 1.125)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may substitute the entire specification by submitting a substitute specification that complies with 37 CFR 1.125(b) and (c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A substitute specification must include a clean version, a separate marked-up version showing changes relative to the previous version, and a statement that the substitute contains no new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation restriction in subsequent amendment documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a paragraph or section is amended in a first amendment document, that paragraph or section shall not be represented in a subsequent amendment document unless it is amended again or a substitute specification is provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid repetition of previously amended paragraphs in later amendment papers to comply with 1.121 processing expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: When applicant may amend (timing rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may amend before or after the first Office action and after the second Office actions as specified in 37 CFR 1.112; after final rejection if amendment meets criteria of 37 CFR 1.116; after filing a notice of appeal if amendment meets 37 CFR 41.33; and when specifically required by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments in provisional applications are not normally made; if made they must comply with 1.121 and will be placed in the provisional file but may not be entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new matter rule
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment may introduce new matter into the disclosure of an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments that add subject matter beyond the original disclosure are prohibited. Substitute specifications must include a statement that no new matter is included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure consistency requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure must be amended, when required by the Office, to correct inaccuracies of description or definition, and to secure substantial correspondence between the claims, the remainder of the specification, and the drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure claims, spec, and drawings correspond; correct inaccuracies when requested to avoid inconsistencies during prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims amendment format: full claim rewrites and complete claim listing
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to a claim must be made by rewriting the entire claim with all changes indicated. Each amendment document that changes claims must include a complete listing of all claims ever presented (pending and withdrawn), with the status of every claim indicated after its claim number by a parenthetical identifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The claim listing replaces prior versions of claims in the application. Claim listing must commence on a separate sheet and include only claim text on the sheets that contain claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim status identifiers and acceptable alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: The status of every claim must be identified by one of the status identifiers: (Original), (Currently amended), (Canceled), (Withdrawn), (Previously presented), (New), or (Not entered). The Office may accept alternative wording if the status is accurate and clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of acceptable alternatives (e.g., 'Original Claim', 'Newly added', 'Canceled without prejudice'). The examiner may accept additional variations; acceptance does not require a corrective amendment or notice to applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markings for amended claims (underlining/strike-through/double brackets)
rubrics_metrics.description: All claims being currently amended must be presented with markings to indicate changes: added matter underlined; deleted matter shown by strike-through. Exceptions: deletion of five or fewer consecutive characters may use double brackets; if strike-through cannot be perceived double brackets must be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only claims with status 'currently amended' or 'withdrawn' (if being amended) include markings. Claims added by amendment must be indicated as 'new' and presented in clean text (no underlining). Do not provide an accompanying clean version of a marked-up claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of claim text not currently amended (clean version) and canceled claims
rubrics_metrics.description: All pending claims not being currently amended must be presented in clean version (no markings); presentation in clean version constitutes an assertion that the claim has not changed relative to the immediate prior version. No claim text shall be presented for canceled or 'not entered' claims—the claim listing should simply identify them by number and status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If canceled or not-entered claims are nevertheless submitted with text, the Office may accept if otherwise compliant with 1.121 to reduce processing time. Reinstatement of previously canceled claims is only by adding the claim as 'new' with a new claim number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim numbering preservation and numbering of new claims (37 CFR 1.126)
rubrics_metrics.description: All claims in each amendment paper must be presented in ascending numerical order. The original numbering of claims must be preserved throughout prosecution; remaining claims must not be renumbered when claims are canceled. New claims must be numbered consecutively beginning with the number next following the highest numbered claim previously presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consecutive canceled or not-entered claims may be aggregated into one statement (e.g., Claims 1–5 (canceled)). Follow 37 CFR 1.126 for numbering practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to drawings: replacement and new sheet rules (37 CFR 1.84)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any changes to application drawings must comply with 37 CFR 1.84 and be submitted on a replacement sheet labeled 'Replacement Sheet' or a 'New Sheet' as appropriate. Replacement sheet must include all figures that appeared on the immediate prior version of the sheet, even if only one figure is amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not label figure or figure number as 'amended'. Include an explanation of changes in the 'Amendments to the Drawings' or the remarks section. A marked-up 'Annotated Sheet' may be included and must be clearly labeled. If examiner requires, a marked-up copy must be provided. No red-ink proposed corrections; proposed correction practice was eliminated and will be treated as non-compliant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing/specification consistency when drawings change
rubrics_metrics.description: If drawing figures are changed, applicant must amend the brief and detailed description of drawings sections of the specification if they are not consistent with the changes to the drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to amend the specification to reflect drawing changes will lead to objections and possible non-entry of changes; if drawing changes not approved, Office will notify in next Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing processing after allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawing submissions without any amendments to the specification and claims after allowance should be forwarded to the Office of Data Management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow filing instructions for post-allowance drawing-only submissions to ensure proper routing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's amendments exception (37 CFR 1.121(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may make examiner's amendments to the specification, including the claims, by specific instructions to insert or delete subject matter at precise locations; examiner's amendments do not need to comply with paragraphs (b)(1), (b)(2), or (c) of 37 CFR 1.121.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner's amendments are used to expedite prosecution and reduce cycle time; applicant should be aware that such changes may be made without the formal amendment markup requirements applicable to applicant-filed amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special appendix and large data amendments must follow their rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes to 'Large Tables' (37 CFR 1.58(c)), 'Computer Program Listing Appendix' (37 CFR 1.96(c)(5) and (7)), 'Sequence Listing' (37 CFR 1.825), or 'Sequence Listing XML' (37 CFR 1.835) must be made in accordance with the specific rules governing those appendices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to amend these items using generic paragraph/section markup—follow the designated regulations to ensure compliance.
